title: top_k, seed and determinism
summary: top_k exists on a few APIs only, seed gives best-effort repeatability on OpenAI Chat Completions, and no major API guarantees identical outputs.
useIf: You need repeatable behaviour for tests, audits or debugging, or you port code that sets top_k or seed.
avoidIf: You expect bit-for-bit reproducibility from a hosted model. Design tests and audits around variance instead.

explain.md: **top_k** limits sampling to the k most probable tokens. It is not in the OpenAI Responses or Chat Completions bodies. Anthropic Messages still lists `top_k`, deprecated, and models released after Opus 4.6 reject it with 400. Gemini exposes `topK` inside `generationConfig` [[r19]] [[tr3]].

**seed** asks the service to sample deterministically. Only Chat Completions has it, and it is marked Beta. Repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should usually match, but determinism is not guaranteed, so watch `system_fingerprint` for backend changes [[r5]]. The Responses API has no `seed`, and Anthropic documents none and says temperature 0.0 is not fully deterministic [[r19]]. Treat determinism as something you measure: run the same request several times, compare the parsed results and track the agreement rate, instead of assuming a flag delivers it.

explain.title: Compatibility layers drop controls
explain.md: Anthropic's OpenAI SDK layer silently ignores `seed`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`, `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `logit_bias`, `response_format`, `reasoning_effort` and `store`. Anthropic says it is for testing, not production [[r36]].

pitfalls.symptom: A test with `seed` and temperature 0 fails intermittently
pitfalls.cause: `seed` is Beta and best effort, and backends change
pitfalls.fix: Assert on parsed fields with a tolerance over repeated runs, and log `system_fingerprint`

pitfalls.cause: `top_k` is deprecated and rejected on models after Opus 4.6
pitfalls.fix: Remove it and control behaviour with prompt, schema and effort

pitfalls.symptom: `seed` has no effect after a migration
pitfalls.cause: The Responses API and the Anthropic compatibility layer do not support it
pitfalls.fix: Remove it and use stored outputs or repeated-run tests

scenarios.title: A flaky extraction test in CI
scenarios.situation: An extraction prompt is tested in CI by comparing the full output string to a saved file. The test fails about one run in ten with no code change.
constraints: The team wants reliable red and green signals
scenarios.question: How do you fix the test?

options.name: Set `seed` and temperature 0 and keep exact string equality
options.why: Both are best effort, so some runs still differ and the test stays flaky.
options.tradeoff: It helps debugging replays, not CI gating.

options.name: Record golden outputs and review diffs by hand
options.why: Catches real regressions and needs no randomness assumptions.

options.name: Pin the model snapshot, parse fields, and assert a pass rate over several runs per case
options.why: It tolerates harmless variance and fails when quality falls, which is what the gate should measure.
options.tradeoff: Several calls per test case raise CI time and cost.

flips.then: Exact equality on the parsed label is fine, with a small retry budget.
Run the repeated-run suite nightly and a single-run smoke test per commit.

scenarios.takeaway: Gate on measured pass rates, not on exact strings from a sampled model.

scenarios.title: Showing a regulator what the assistant said
scenarios.situation: A regulated team must show exactly what the assistant told a customer last quarter. A colleague suggests regenerating the answer at audit time with `seed` and temperature 0.
constraints: Models and backends change over a quarter
unknowns: Whether the model alias has moved
scenarios.question: What is the sound approach?

options.name: Store inputs, model version, parameters and the output, and show the stored record
options.why: A stored record is exact, while regeneration depends on a model and backend that may have changed.
options.tradeoff: You take on storage, access control and retention duties.

options.name: Send `seed`, log `system_fingerprint`, and regenerate if the fingerprint matches
options.why: A matching fingerprint raises confidence in a replay.
options.tradeoff: Still best effort, and the snapshot may be retired by then.

options.name: Regenerate at audit time with temperature 0
options.why: Temperature 0 is not fully deterministic and the model may have changed.
options.tradeoff: Fine for debugging a recent session, not as evidence.

flips.if: Data retention rules forbid storing outputs
flips.then: Store a hash and the minimum metadata, and consult legal on what proof is acceptable.

flips.if: Only an informal internal review is needed
flips.then: A seeded replay may be enough.

scenarios.takeaway: Evidence is a record, not a recipe you hope to replay.

quiz.q: Match each API to its status for `seed`.
quiz.explain: Only Chat Completions exposes `seed`, and it is Beta. The Responses API and the Anthropic Messages API have none, and the Anthropic compatibility layer silently ignores it.

quiz.q: What is the most defensible way to prove what an assistant said last quarter?
options: Store the output with inputs and model version
Re-run the prompt on the newest model
quiz.explain: A stored record is exact. Regeneration depends on a model and backend that may have changed, and `seed` and temperature 0 are best effort.

quiz.q: Which field helps you notice that the backend changed between two requests with the same seed?
quiz.explain: `system_fingerprint` identifies the backend configuration, so a change explains different outputs. The other fields do not describe the backend.

flashcards.back: Not OpenAI Responses or Chat Completions. Anthropic lists it as deprecated and rejects it on models after Opus 4.6. Gemini has `topK` in `generationConfig`.
Best effort and Beta, on Chat Completions only. Log `system_fingerprint` to spot backend changes.

flashcards.front: How do you test a flaky structured extraction?
flashcards.back: Pin the model snapshot, parse fields, run each case several times and assert a pass rate instead of exact strings.
